items.title: AIで求人業務を効率化する方法10選！採用担当の工数を減らす進め方
items.description: 求人票の作成、応募者への返信、面接の日程調整に追われ、候補者と向き合う時間が取れない。他業務と兼務で採用を担う担当者ほど、この悩みを抱えやすいでしょう。 求人業務のうちAIに任せられる工程は、求人票の作成から採用データの分析まで10あります。なかでも 選考判断の前後にある連絡や記録の作業 から任せると、工数が減りやすくなります。 返信や日程調整が遅れるほど、候補者は先に連絡をくれた他社へ流れます。定型作業をAIに渡せば、面接や候補者の口説きに時間を回せます。 本記事では、工程別のAI活用法10選と、着手する工程を決めて効果を測るまでの5ステップを中心に解説します。 読み終える頃には、自社で最初にAIに任せる工程と、成果を上司に報告するための指標を決められるようになります。 AIで求人業務を効率化できる工程10選 求人業務のうち、AIで効率化できる工程は以下の10個です。 求人票の作成 媒体別の原稿展開 スカウト文面の作成 応募者からの問い合わせ対応 書類選考の一次確認 面接の日程調整 面接の記録と要約 評価シートと面接質問の作成 合否連絡と内定者フォロー 採用データの集計と分析 各工程でAIが担う作業と人が担う作業を分けて押さえると、任せすぎによる失敗を防げます。 求人票の作成 求人票は、 募集要件のメモからAIに初稿を書かせる ことで作成時間を短縮できます。白紙から文章を組み立てる時間が、もっとも工数を使う部分だからです。 たとえば職種名、業務内容、必須スキル、給与、勤務地を箇条書きで渡せば、ChatGPTやGeminiが求人票の形式に整えます。過去に応募が多かった求人票を参考として渡すと、自社らしい表現に近づきます。 一方、給与や労働条件の正確さ、仕事の魅力の打ち出し方は人が確認します。初稿づくりをAIに任せる分、現場社員へのヒアリングに時間を使えば、応募者に響く求人票に仕上げられます。 媒体別の原稿展開 1本の求人票をもとに、 媒体ごとの文字数や形式に合わせた原稿 をAIで書き分けられます。複数の求人媒体や自社採用サイトに掲載する企業ほど、書き直しの手間が積み上がるためです。 たとえば「キャッチコピーは30文字以内」「仕事内容は400文字以内」のように媒体の制約を指示すれば、AIが要約や言い換えをします。SNS向けの短い告知文も、同じ元原稿から作れます。 人が担うのは、書き分けた原稿で条件が食い違っていないかの確認です。元原稿を1本に絞って管理すれば、条件変更の反映漏れも防げます。 スカウト文面の作成 スカウトメールは、 候補者のプロフィールに合わせた個別文面 をAIに下書きさせると効率化できます。定型文の一斉送信では返信率が上がらず、1通ずつ書くと時間が足りないためです。 候補者の職務経歴の要点と自社求人の特徴を渡し、「経歴のどこに注目したかを冒頭で伝える」と指示すれば、AIが個別の書き出しを作ります。スカウト機能にAIを組み込んだ求人媒体や採用管理システムもあります。 送信する候補者の選定と、文面が経歴を誤って解釈していないかの確認は人が行います。下書きの時間が減れば、同じ時間で送れるスカウトの数を増やせます。 応募者からの問い合わせ対応 選考の流れや勤務条件に関する問い合わせは、 AIチャットボットで一次回答 できます。応募者の質問の多くは、求人票や採用サイトに答えがある定型的な内容だからです。 たとえば「リモート勤務は可能か」「選考は何回あるか」といった質問に、チャットボットが夜間や休日も自動で答えます。回答できない質問だけを担当者に引き継ぐ設定にすれば、担当者が対応する件数を絞れます。 人が担うのは、回答の元になるFAQの整備と、個別事情を含む相談への対応です。応募者を待たせない体制は、応募の取りこぼしを減らすことにもつながります。 書類選考の一次確認 書類選考では、 必須要件を満たしているかの照合と経歴の要約 をAIに任せられます。履歴書と職務経歴書を1通ずつ読み込む作業は、応募数に比例して時間が増えるためです。 たとえば「法人営業の経験3年以上」「普通自動車免許」といった要件を渡すと、AIが該当箇所を抜き出して一覧にします。担当者は要約を読んでから、気になる応募者の書類だけを詳しく確認できます。 ただし、合否の判断はAIに任せきりにせず人が行います。AIの照合結果を判断材料として使えば、確認の速さと判断の納得感を両立できます。 面接の日程調整 面接の日程調整は、 日程調整ツールとAIの組み合わせで自動化 しやすい工程です。候補日の提示、面接官の空き確認、確定連絡というやり取りの往復が、担当者の時間を細かく奪うためです。 面接官のカレンダーと連携した日程調整ツールを使えば、応募者が空き枠から希望日時を選ぶだけで予約が確定します。AIは日程変更の依頼メールを読み取り、返信文を下書きする役割を担えます。 人が担うのは、面接官の調整がつかない場合の個別対応です。応募から面接までの日数が縮まれば、候補者の志望度が高いうちに会えます。 面接の記録と要約 面接の内容は、 文字起こしと要約をAIに任せる ことで記録の手間を減らせます。面接中のメモ取りと面接後の清書は、面接官と担当者の双方に負担がかかるためです。 オンライン面接の録画や録音をAIで文字起こしし、「志望動機」「強み」「懸念点」の項目ごとに要約させれば、社内共有用の記録ができます。面接官はメモ取りから解放され、候補者との対話に集中できます。 録音や録画をする場合は、事前に候補者の同意を取ることが前提です。記録の質がそろえば、次の選考に進む面接官への引き継ぎもスムーズになります。 評価シートと面接質問の作成 評価シートと面接質問は、 求める人物像からAIに案を出させる と短時間で用意できます。職種ごとにゼロから評価項目を考えるのは、採用担当者にとって負担が大きい作業です。 たとえば「顧客折衝力」「チームでの課題解決」といった評価軸を渡すと、AIが評価基準と、それを確かめる行動事実の質問例を作ります。面接官ごとに質問がばらつく問題も抑えられます。 質問案のうち、職務と関係のない家族構成や出身地などを尋ねる内容が混ざっていないかは人が確認します。公正な選考の土台を整えることは、採用の質を保つことに直結します。 合否連絡と内定者フォロー 合否連絡や内定者へのフォローメールは、 AIで下書きを作って送信漏れを防ぐ ことで効率化できます。選考段階ごとに文面を書き分ける作業は、応募者が増えるほど遅れの原因になるためです。 不合格通知は応募者への配慮を保った定型文を、内定者フォローは入社までの手続きや懇親会の案内を、それぞれAIで作れます。採用管理システムと連携すれば、選考ステータスの変更に合わせて送信できます。 内定辞退の兆候がある候補者への連絡は、人が直接行います。定型連絡をAIに任せた分、内定者一人ひとりとの面談に時間を割けます。 採用データの集計と分析 媒体別の応募数や選考通過率は、 AIに集計と傾向の読み取りを任せられます 。表計算ソフトで手作業で集計していると、分析の前に時間切れになりやすいためです。 採用管理システムから書き出したCSVをChatGPTなどに読み込ませ、「媒体別の応募から内定までの通過率を出して」と指示すれば、集計表とグラフができます。どの媒体に予算を寄せるべきかを考える材料になります。 応募者の氏名などの個人情報は、読み込ませる前に削除します。データにもとづく改善が回り始めると、採用活動全体の精度が上がります。 求人業務で時間を奪っているのは判断の前後にある作業 採用担当者の時間を奪っているのは、合否の判断そのものではなく、その前後に発生する以下の3つの作業です。 日程調整と連絡の往復 面接後の記録と共有 社内の合否判断と条件調整 この3つの作業の実態を知ると、AIに最初に任せるべき工程が見えてきます。 日程調整と連絡の往復 日程調整は、 作業を分けて数えると想定より時間がかかる 工程です。1回ごとの作業は短くても、候補日の提示から確定連絡まで複数のやり取りが重なるためです。 株式会社ゼクウが採用担当者・人事責任者1,002名に実施した調査では、応募者1名への対応時間をまとめて尋ねた場合の中央値は約10分でした。一方、日程調整を候補日提示、面接官の空き確認、変更対応、確定連絡に分けて尋ねると、中央値は約14分でした。 出典： 採用業務の「見えない工数」実態調査2026（日本の人事部） 担当者の感覚よりも、細かな作業の積み重ねが工数を押し上げています。日程調整を自動化の候補に挙げれば、見えにくかった時間を取り戻せます。 面接後の記録と共有 面接後の記録と共有も、 選考判断の後ろで工数を生む作業 です。面接の内容を清書し、関係者に共有して評価をそろえるまでに、面接そのものとは別の時間がかかります。 前述のゼクウの調査でも、時間がかかる工程として面談後の記録、日程調整、連絡の往復が上位に挙がっています。また、HeaR株式会社は中途採用の書類選考を7工程・55タスクに分解し、合否を決める意思決定は1タスクのみで、連絡が19タスクを占めると公表しています。 出典： 書類選考55タスク分解レポート（HeaR株式会社） 判断以外の作業は手順が決まっているため、AIに任せやすい領域です。記録と共有を効率化すれば、面接官の負担も同時に軽くできます。 社内の合否判断と条件調整 選考が滞る最大の原因は、 社内の合否判断と条件調整 です。面接官や配属部署の確認待ちが発生すると、担当者が催促と再調整に追われます。 ゼクウの調査では、選考が滞る原因として「社内の合否判断・条件調整」が40.2%で最多、「日程調整」が37.3%で続きました。 出典： 採用業務の「見えない工数」実態調査2026（日本の人事部） 判断そのものは人が行いますが、AIは面接記録の要約や候補者の比較表を作り、判断材料をそろえる役割を担えます。判断に必要な情報が一目でわかれば、確認待ちの時間を縮められます。 AIで求人業務を効率化する4つのメリット AIで求人業務を効率化するメリットは、以下の4つです。 定型作業の工数を減らせる 応募から内定までの期間を短縮できる 担当者による品質のばらつきを抑えられる 夜間や休日も応募者に対応できる メリットを具体的に言語化しておくと、社内でAI導入の合意を得やすくなります。 定型作業の工数を減らせる AI活用の最大のメリットは、 手順が決まった作業の時間を減らせる ことです。求人票の初稿、連絡メール、面接記録の清書は、毎回同じ手順を繰り返す作業だからです。 たとえば合否連絡のメールを選考段階ごとにテンプレート化し、AIで候補者名や日程を差し込めば、1通ずつ文面を考える必要がなくなります。兼務の担当者ほど、細切れの作業が減る効果を実感しやすいでしょう。 浮いた時間は、候補者との面談や現場とのすり合わせに回せます。採用担当者が本来の役割である候補者の見極めと口説きに集中できる状態をつくれます。 応募から内定までの期間を短縮できる AIを使うと、 応募から内定までの各段階の待ち時間 を縮められます。書類確認や日程調整の遅れが、選考全体の期間を延ばす原因になっているためです。 書類選考の要約をAIが当日中に作り、面接日程を応募者が自分で予約できる状態にすれば、応募から一次面接までの日数が縮まります。複数社を並行して受ける候補者にとって、早い連絡は企業を選ぶ判断材料の1つです。 選考期間が短くなれば、他社に先を越されて辞退される機会も減ります。採用競争が激しい職種ほど、スピードの差が採用成果の差として表れます。 担当者による品質のばらつきを抑えられる AIを使うと、 求人票や面接評価の品質を一定にそろえやすく なります。同じ指示文やテンプレートを使えば、担当者が変わっても出力の形式と項目が統一されるためです。 たとえば求人票作成用の指示文に「仕事内容」「必須スキル」「歓迎スキル」「労働条件」の項目を固定しておけば、記載漏れが起きにくくなります。面接の評価シートも、評価軸と基準をAIで整えると面接官ごとの差が縮まります。 品質がそろうと、特定の担当者に業務が依存する属人化も解消に向かいます。異動や退職があっても採用の質を保てる体制は、組織にとって大きな安心材料です。 夜間や休日も応募者に対応できる AIチャットボットを使えば、 担当者の勤務時間外も応募者に対応 できます。在職中の転職希望者は、仕事を終えた夜間や休日に求人を探して応募することが多いためです。 夜間に届いた問い合わせにチャットボットが即座に答え、そのまま面接予約まで案内すれば、翌営業日まで応募者を待たせずに済みます。担当者は出勤後に、AIが対応しきれなかった案件だけを確認します。 応募者が関心を持った瞬間に応答できる体制は、応募意欲が冷める前に選考へ進んでもらうことにつながります。担当者の残業を増やさずに対応時間を広げられる点も、兼務の担当者には大きな利点です。 AIで求人業務を効率化する5ステップ AIで求人業務を効率化するには、以下の5ステップで進めます。 採用工程ごとの工数を棚卸しする 最初にAIに任せる工程を決める 工程に合ったツールを選ぶ 1職種・1工程で小さく試す 効果を測ってほかの工程に広げる いきなりツールを導入すると、工数が減らない工程にAIを入れてしまう失敗が起こります。 ステップ1：採用工程ごとの工数を棚卸しする 最初に、 採用工程ごとに1か月あたりの作業時間を書き出します 。どこに時間がかかっているかを把握しないと、効果の大きい工程を選べないためです。 前述の10工程を表の行に並べ、「1件あたりの作業時間」と「月の件数」を記入して掛け合わせます。日程調整のように細かな作業が重なる工程は、候補日の提示、面接官の空き確認、確定連絡のように作業を分けて記録すると実態に近づきます。 1〜2週間ほど実際の作業時間を記録すると、より正確な数値になります。棚卸しの結果は、導入後の効果を比べる基準値としてそのまま使えます。 ステップ2：最初にAIに任せる工程を決める 最初にAIに任せる工程は、 工数が大きく、手順が決まっていて、合否の判断を含まない工程 から選びます。この3条件を満たす工程は、AIに任せても失敗したときの影響が小さく、効果も見えやすいた

items.title: AI原稿作成のやり方を解説！種類別プロンプト例とおすすめツール6選
items.description: 発表資料やプレスリリースの締め切りが重なり、原稿をゼロから書く時間が足りないと感じている方は多いでしょう。ChatGPTに頼んでみたものの、硬い文章しか出てこず書き直した経験がある方もいるのではないでしょうか。 AIで原稿を作るときは、目的・読み手・素材を渡し、本文より先に構成を作らせると、手直しの少ない下書きが得られます。 「原稿を書いて」と頼むだけでは、誰にでも当てはまる一般的な文章になり、書き直しの手間は減りません。誤情報や他者の表現に似た文章をそのまま社外に出せば、会社の信用にも関わります。 本記事では、AIで原稿を作る5つの手順と、プレゼン・スピーチ・求人など原稿の種類別のプロンプト例を中心に解説します。 読み終えたときには、自分の原稿に合った指示で下書きを作り、事実確認まで済ませて提出できる状態になっています。ぜひ最後までご覧ください。 AIで原稿を作成する5ステップ AIで原稿を作成する手順は、以下の5ステップです。 原稿の目的と読み手を決める AIに渡す素材を集める 構成案を先に作らせる 構成に沿って本文を生成する 事実確認と自分の言葉で仕上げる 本文を書かせる前の準備と、生成後の仕上げに手間をかけるほど、書き直しの量は減ります。 ステップ1：原稿の目的と読み手を決める 最初に、 原稿の目的・読み手・分量の3点を言葉にしておきます 。AIは指示にない情報を一般論で補うため、この3点が曖昧だと誰にでも当てはまる文章になるからです。 目的は「新サービスへの問い合わせを増やす」「新入社員の不安を和らげる」のように、読み手にとってほしい行動まで書きます。読み手は役職や知識レベルまで具体的にするほど、言葉選びが合ってきます。 分量は、読む原稿なら文字数、話す原稿なら持ち時間で決めます。プレゼンやスピーチは 話す時間を基準にする と、当日の時間超過を防げます。 この3点は、後のステップでプロンプトにそのまま貼り付けて使えます。最初に5分かけて整理しておくと、AIとのやり取りの往復回数が減ります。 ステップ2：AIに渡す素材を集める 次に、原稿の中身になる素材を集めます。 AIが知らない社内の事実や数値は、素材として渡さない限り原稿に入りません 。 集めておきたい素材は以下のとおりです。 伝えたい要点を書き出した箇条書きのメモ 発表に使うスライドや企画書 過去に書いた同じ種類の原稿 数値・日付・固有名詞などの確定情報 自分の体験や具体的なエピソード とくにエピソードは、AIが最も作れない部分です。素材が少ないまま生成すると、AIはもっともらしい架空の話で埋めることがあります。 ただし、未発表の情報や個人情報を含む素材は、入力してよいかを先に確認してください。入力ルールは後述の注意点で解説しています。 ステップ3：構成案を先に作らせる 素材がそろったら、本文ではなく 見出しや話の流れだけを先に出力させます 。構成の段階で直すほうが、本文を書き直すより手間が小さいからです。 指示は以下のように、ステップ1の3点と素材を渡したうえで、構成だけを求めます。 以下の条件で原稿の構成案を作成してください。本文はまだ書かないでください。 # 目的 【例：新サービスへの問い合わせを増やす】 # 読み手 【例：中小企業の総務担当者。AIの知識は少ない】 # 分量 【例：1,500字】 # 素材 【メモ・スライドの内容を貼り付け】 # 出力形式 見出しと、各見出しで伝える要点を1〜2行で示してください。 出てきた構成は、順番の入れ替えや不要な見出しの削除など、人が判断して整えます。 伝える順番を自分で決めておく と、本文の論理が崩れにくくなります。 ステップ4：構成に沿って本文を生成する 整えた構成を渡し、本文を生成させます。 長い原稿は見出しごとに分けて生成する と、内容の薄い段落や途中での話の脱線が減ります。 本文を頼む際は、文体と避けたい表現もあわせて指定します。たとえば「ですます調」「1文は60字以内」「専門用語には説明を添える」などです。 先ほどの構成のうち、見出し1の本文を書いてください。 # 条件 ・文体：ですます調 ・1文は60字以内 ・専門用語には短い説明を添える ・素材にない数値や事例は書かず、必要な箇所は【要確認】と記載する 最後の条件のように、素材にない情報を書かせない指示を入れておくと、確認すべき箇所が一目でわかります。仕上げの作業が楽になる指示です。 ステップ5：事実確認と自分の言葉で仕上げる 生成された本文は下書きとして扱い、 事実確認と言い回しの修正を人が行って完成させます 。AIの文章には事実と異なる内容や、AI特有の言い回しが残るからです。 事実確認では、数値・日付・固有名詞・引用を、公式発表などの一次情報と1件ずつ照合します。そのうえで、以下の観点でAIくささを消していきます。 チェック項目 直し方 同じ語尾が3文以上続いている 体言を主語にする・文をつなげるなどで語尾を変える 「さまざまな」「重要です」など抽象的な言葉が多い 具体的な数値・名称・場面に置き換える 前置きや締めの一文が毎段落にある 結論から書き、繰り返しの締めを削る 自分の体験や社内の固有の話がない エピソードを1つ以上自分で足す 声に出すと詰まる箇所がある 音読して、言いにくい箇所を自分の話し方に直す とくにスピーチやプレゼンの原稿は、必ず一度声に出して読みます。耳で聞いて自然な文章に直すことで、自分の言葉として話せる原稿に仕上がります。 原稿の種類別AIプロンプト例7選 原稿の種類ごとにそのまま使えるプロンプト例を、以下の7つ紹介します。 プレゼン原稿 スピーチ原稿 記事・ブログ原稿 プレスリリース 求人原稿 社内報・メルマガ 動画台本 原稿の種類によって指定すべき項目は変わるため、自分が書く原稿の例から読み進めてください。 【プレゼン原稿】スライドから発表原稿を作る プレゼン原稿は、 スライドの内容と持ち時間を渡し、スライドごとに区切って出力させる のがポイントです。区切っておくと、発表中にどのスライドで何を話すかが迷わずわかります。 あなたは社内プレゼンの原稿作成を支援するアシスタントです。 以下のスライド内容をもとに、話し言葉の発表原稿を作成してください。 # 発表の目的 【例：来期の予算増額を承認してもらう】 # 聞き手 【例：経営層5名】 # 持ち時間 【例：10分】 # スライド内容 【スライド1〜10のテキストを貼り付け】 # 条件 ・スライドごとに見出しを付けて区切る ・話し言葉のですます調 ・スライドに書いてある文をそのまま読み上げる構成にしない 最後の条件を入れると、スライドの文字を読み上げるだけの原稿になるのを防げます。スライドに書けなかった背景や根拠を話す原稿になり、聞き手の納得感が高まります。 【スピーチ原稿】朝礼や式典の挨拶を作る スピーチ原稿では、 自分で用意したエピソードを必ず素材に入れます 。エピソードがないと、AIはどの会社でも使える一般的な挨拶を作ってしまうからです。 以下の条件で、スピーチ原稿を作成してください。 # 場面 【例：入社式での部長挨拶】 # 聞き手 【例：新入社員30名】 # 持ち時間 【例：3分】 # 伝えたいこと 【例：失敗を恐れず質問してほしい】 # 入れたいエピソード 【例：自分が新人時代に質問できず、納期を1週間遅らせた経験】 # 条件 ・話し言葉で、聞き手に語りかける口調 ・冒頭30秒でエピソードに入る ・最後は聞き手への期待で締める 朝礼・送別会・表彰式など場面が変わっても、場面と伝えたいことを差し替えるだけで使えます。 話し手の体験が入った原稿 は、聞き手の記憶に残りやすくなります。 【記事・ブログ原稿】オウンドメディアの記事を作る 記事・ブログ原稿は、 構成の作成と本文の作成を2回に分けて依頼します 。1回で全文を書かせると、見出し同士で内容が重なったり、後半の情報が薄くなったりしやすいからです。 オウンドメディアに掲載する記事の構成案を作成してください。 # テーマ 【例：中小企業がクラウド会計を選ぶポイント】 # 想定読者 【例：従業員30名以下の企業の経理担当者】 # 読者の悩み 【例：ツールが多く、どれを選べばよいかわからない】 # 文字数 【例：4,000字】 # 条件 ・見出しはH2とH3で構成する ・各見出しで伝える要点を1行で添える 構成を確認・修正したら、ステップ4のプロンプトで見出しごとに本文を生成します。読者の悩みを書いておくと、悩みの解決から逆算した構成が出てきます。 【プレスリリース】新サービスの発表文を作る プレスリリースは、 5W1Hと数値を素材として渡し、リリースの型で出力させます 。記者が必要な情報を探しやすい型に沿うことで、記事化の判断材料をそろえられるからです。 以下の情報をもとに、プレスリリースの原稿を作成してください。 # 発表内容（5W1H） ・誰が：【社名】 ・何を：【サービス名と概要】 ・いつ：【提供開始日】 ・どこで：【提供地域・チャネル】 ・なぜ：【開発の背景となる課題】 ・どのように：【提供方法・料金】 # 数値情報 【例：導入テストでの成果、価格など】 # 代表者コメント 【箇条書きで要点を記載】 # 出力形式 タイトル、リード文、本文、会社概要の順で作成してください。 素材にない数値は書かないでください。 代表者コメントは、AIに作らせた文章をそのまま載せず、本人に確認を取ってください。 素材にない数値を書かせない指示 を入れておくと、誤った数字が社外に出るリスクを抑えられます。 【求人原稿】募集職種の紹介文を作る 求人原稿は、仕事内容と働く魅力を渡したうえで、 法令で求められる明示事項が抜けていないかを人が確認します 。AIは法改正を反映していない場合があるからです。 以下の情報をもとに、求人サイトに掲載する求人原稿を作成してください。 # 職種 【例：法人営業】 # 仕事内容 【1日の流れ、担当する顧客、使うツールなど】 # 応募条件 【必須条件・歓迎条件】 # 働き方・待遇 【勤務地、勤務時間、給与、休日】 # この仕事の魅力 【現場社員の声など】 # 条件 ・求職者が入社後の1日を想像できる書き方にする ・性別や年齢を限定する表現は使わない 2024年4月から、募集時に「従事すべき業務の変更の範囲」「就業の場所の変更の範囲」なども明示が必要になりました。生成後に、明示事項がそろっているかを確認してください。 出典： 令和６年４月より、募集時等に明示すべき事項が追加されます（厚生労働省） 【社内報・メルマガ】社内外へのお知らせを作る 社内報やメルマガは、 伝えたい事実と読み手の関心をセットで渡す のがポイントです。事実だけを渡すと、読み手にとっての意味が書かれない事務連絡のような文章になるからです。 以下の内容で、社内報の記事を作成してください。 # 伝えたい事実 【例：4月から経費精算システムが新しくなる】 # 読み手 【例：全社員。毎月の経費精算に手間を感じている】 # 読み手にとってのメリット 【例：スマホで領収書を撮影するだけで申請できる】 # トーン 【例：親しみやすく、ですます調】 # 文字数 【例：600字】 # 条件 ・冒頭で読み手のメリットを伝える ・手続きの期限と問い合わせ先を最後に記載する メルマガの場合は、件名の案を5つほど同時に出させると、開封されやすい件名を選べます。冒頭で読み手のメリットを伝える構成にすると、最後まで読まれやすくなります。 【動画台本】ナレーション原稿を作る 動画台本は、 ナレーションとテロップを分けて出力させます 。耳で聞く言葉と画面で読む言葉は、適した長さや言い回しが違うからです。 以下の条件で、動画の台本を作成してください。 # 動画の目的 【例：新サービスの使い方を紹介する】 # 視聴者 【例：サービスを申し込んだばかりの担当者】 # 尺 【例：2分】 # 映像の流れ 【例：ログイン画面→初期設定→レポート画面】 # 出力形式 表形式で「時間」「映像」「ナレーション」「テロップ」の4列に分けてください。 表形式で出力させると、撮影や編集の担当者とそのまま共有できます。完成した台本は、実際に声に出して尺に収まるかを確かめてから撮影に進んでください。 AI原稿の質を上げるプロンプトのコツ6つ AI原稿の質を上げるプロンプトのコツは、以下の6つです。 AIに役割を与える 読み手と目的を具体的に書く 文字数や話す時間を指定する お手本の文章を渡す 使わない表現を指定する 対話で修正を重ねる プロンプト例を自分用に調整するときの判断基準として活用してください。 AIに役割を与える プロンプトの冒頭で 「あなたは〇〇の担当者です」と役割を与える と、原稿の視点と言葉選びがそろいます。役割に合わせて、AIが想定する読み手や専門用語の扱いが変わるからです。 たとえば同じ新サービスの紹介でも、「広報担当者」なら社外向けの客観的な文章になります。「営業担当者」なら顧客の課題に寄り添う提案調の文章になります。 役割は「BtoB企業で10年働く広報担当者」のように、経験や業界まで加えるとより具体的になります。原稿の種類に合った役割を選ぶことで、書き直す前の段階から自社らしい文章に近づきます。 読み手と目的を具体的に書く 読み手と目的は、 1文で具体的に書く ほど原稿の精度が上がります。読み手が曖昧なまま生成すると、AIは最も一般的な読み手を想定するからです。 曖昧な指定 具体的な指定 社員向けに 入社3年目までの営業担当者向けに サービスを紹介して 無料トライアルへの申し込みを促して わかりやすく AIを使ったことがない人にもわかるように 目的には、読み終えた人にとってほしい行動まで含めます。行動が決まると、AIは結論や締めの一文をその行動に向けて書くようになります。 文字数や話す時間を指定する 原稿の分量は、 文字数か話す時間で必ず指定します 。指定がないと、AIは用途に対して長すぎる、または短すぎる原稿を出すことがあるからです。 ただし、AIは指定した文字数をぴったり守るのが得意ではありません。生成後に文字数カウントで確認し、ずれていれば「あと300字短くして」のように調整を頼みます。 話す原稿は、自分の話す速さ

items.title: 営業でAIを活用する方法10選！導入事例・失敗しない始め方を解説
items.description: 経営層から「営業でもAIを活用しよう」と言われたものの、ChatGPTでメール文を作る以外の使い道が思いつかない方は多いでしょう。何から手を付けるべきか、迷っている方もいるのではないでしょうか。 AI営業とは、営業プロセスの事務作業や分析をAIに任せ、営業担当者が顧客と向き合う時間を増やす取り組みです。 日本の営業担当者が営業活動に費やす時間は44%にとどまるという調査があります。入力や議事録に追われたままでは、AIで商談数を伸ばす競合との差は開く一方でしょう。 本記事では、営業プロセスの工程別に整理したAIの活用方法10選と、公式発表で成果を確認できる導入事例6選を中心に解説します。 読み終えたときには、自社のどの工程からAIを入れるべきかを判断し、導入計画を描ける状態になっています。ぜひ最後までご覧ください。 AI営業とは？営業プロセスにAIを組み込む取り組み AI営業とは、リスト作成から商談後の記録、育成までの営業プロセスにAIを組み込み、事務作業の自動化と判断の精度向上を図る取り組みです。AI営業を理解するために押さえたいポイントは以下の3つです。 AI営業の定義 予測AI・生成AI・AIエージェントの違い AI営業が注目される背景 3つを押さえておくと、後半で紹介する活用方法やツールを自社に当てはめて読めるようになります。 AI営業の定義 AI営業とは、特定のツール名ではなく、営業の各工程でAIを使う取り組みの総称です。 営業の仕事は、見込み客を探す段階から、提案・商談・受注後のフォローまで多くの工程に分かれます。AI営業では、工程ごとに向いているAIを使い分け、人が担っていた作業の一部をAIに任せます。 よく混同されるのが、SFA（営業支援システム）やCRM（顧客管理システム）との違いです。SFA・CRMは営業活動を 記録・管理する仕組み であり、AIは記録されたデータを分析したり、文章を生成したり、作業を実行したりする役割を担います。 最近はSFA・CRMにAIが搭載されるケースが増え、両者の境目は薄れています。AI営業を「SFA・CRMに貯まったデータを、AIで成果に変える取り組み」と捉えると、自社の現状から何を足すべきかが見えてきます。 予測AI・生成AI・AIエージェントの違い 営業で使われるAIは、予測AI・生成AI・AIエージェントの3種類に分けられます。 3種類は得意な作業がまったく異なるため、違いを理解せずにツールを選ぶと、課題に合わないAIを導入してしまいます。それぞれの特徴は以下のとおりです。 種類 得意な作業 営業での使い道の例 人の関与 予測AI 過去データから確率や数値を予測する 見込み客のスコアリング・売上予測 予測結果を見て人が判断する 生成AI 文章・資料・要約を作成する 営業メール・提案資料・議事録の作成 生成物を人が確認・修正する AIエージェント 複数の作業を自律的に実行する 情報収集からSFA入力・フォロー文面作成まで 人は指示と最終確認を行う たとえば、見込み客の優先順位付けは予測AI、メール作成は生成AI、商談後の入力からフォローまでの一連の作業はAIエージェントが向いています。 自社の課題が「判断」「作成」「作業の連続」のどれにあるかを考えると、どの種類のAIから試すべきかを絞り込めます。 AI営業が注目される背景 AI営業が注目される最大の理由は、 営業担当者が本来の営業活動に使える時間が限られている ことです。 Salesforceの調査『営業最新事情（第7版）』では、営業担当者が営業活動に費やす時間は平均40%で、日本では44%にとどまっています。残りの時間は、データ入力や社内調整などの業務に使われていることになります。 出典： 世界の営業職4,000人以上を対象とした『営業最新事情』（第7版）を発表（Salesforce） 同じ調査では、日本の営業プロフェッショナルの62%が見込み顧客開拓にAIを活用し、31%が将来的に活用する予定と回答しています。 AI活用はすでに一部の先進企業だけの取り組みではありません。 人手不足で営業人員を簡単に増やせない中、AIで1人あたりの営業時間を取り戻すことは、売上を伸ばすための現実的な手段になっています。 AIを営業に活用する方法10選 AIを営業に活用する方法は、営業プロセスの工程ごとに以下の10個があります。 【リード獲得】営業リストを自動で作成する 【リード獲得】見込み客をスコアリングする 【アプローチ】営業メールを顧客ごとに作成する 【アプローチ】AIコールで架電を自動化する 【商談準備】顧客企業の情報を調べる 【商談準備】提案資料を作成する 【商談】商談を文字起こし・要約する 【商談後】SFA・CRMへの入力を自動化する 【管理】売上を予測する 【育成】AIロープレで営業スキルを鍛える 自社で時間がかかっている工程から読むと、AIを導入すべき優先順位がわかります。 【リード獲得】営業リストを自動で作成する 企業データベースとAIを組み合わせると、ターゲット条件に合う営業リストを自動で作成できます。 従来のリスト作成は、企業サイトや求人媒体を1社ずつ調べる手作業が中心でした。担当者によって抽出基準もばらつき、リストの質が安定しないという課題がありました。 営業リスト作成ツールでは、業種・従業員数・所在地に加えて、採用の動きやニュースといった「今まさに動いている企業」の兆候も条件に入れられます。たとえばMusubuは、1,200万件の法人データとニュース・求人などの動的データから、アプローチ先とタイミングを検知すると公式サイトで説明しています。 >Musubuの公式サイトは こちらから リスト作成の時間を減らせば、その分を架電や提案の準備に回せます。 【リード獲得】見込み客をスコアリングする AIによるスコアリングでは、見込み客ごとの成約しやすさを点数化し、アプローチの優先順位を決められます。 見込み客が増えるほど、すべてに同じ熱量で対応するのは難しくなります。経験豊富な営業担当者は勘で優先順位を付けていますが、その判断基準はチームで共有しにくいものです。 AIは、過去の受注・失注データと、Webサイトの閲覧履歴や資料ダウンロードなどの行動データを照らし合わせ、成約に近い見込み客を見つけ出します。MAツールやSFA・CRMの多くが、スコアリング機能を備えています。 ただし、スコアは過去データにもとづく予測にすぎません。 スコアを参考にしつつ、最終的な優先順位は営業担当者が判断する 運用にすると、取りこぼしを防げます。 【アプローチ】営業メールを顧客ごとに作成する 生成AIを使うと、顧客ごとに内容を変えた営業メールを短時間で作成できます。 テンプレートの一斉送信は手間がかからない一方、受け手には「自分宛てではない」と見抜かれやすく、返信率が伸び悩みます。かといって1通ずつ書き分けるには、多くの時間が必要です。 生成AIに顧客の業種・課題の仮説・過去のやりとりを渡せば、件名と本文を顧客ごとに作り分けた下書きが数十秒で完成します。ChatGPTやMicrosoft 365 Copilot、Geminiなどの汎用的な生成AIで対応できます。 送信前には、社名・担当者名・数値などの事実関係と、自社らしい言葉づかいになっているかを人が確認しましょう。確認の工程を残すことで、AIで速度を上げながら信頼を損なわないメール運用ができます。 【アプローチ】AIコールで架電を自動化する AIコールとは、AIが音声で電話をかけ、ヒアリングやアポイントの打診を行う仕組みです。 架電は営業担当者の負担が大きい業務の1つです。Salesforceの同調査でも、日本の営業担当者の52%が「新規顧客への電話アプローチが仕事で最も苦痛な作業」と回答しています。 出典： 世界の営業職4,000人以上を対象とした『営業最新事情』（第7版）を発表（Salesforce） AIコールでは、AIが一次架電で相手の関心度を確かめ、見込みのある相手だけを営業担当者に引き継ぎます。海外ではElevenLabsが、リードの選別やアポイント設定、フォローアップを電話やメッセージで自動化するAIエージェントを提供しています。 >ElevenLabsの公式サイトは こちらから 向いているのは、休眠顧客の掘り起こしやセミナー参加者へのフォローなど、すでに接点のある相手への架電です。面識のない相手への新規架電は受け手の不信感を招きやすいため、後半で解説する注意点も確認したうえで導入を検討しましょう。 【商談準備】顧客企業の情報を調べる 生成AIやAIエージェントを使うと、商談前の企業リサーチと課題の仮説づくりを短時間で済ませられます。 商談の質は事前準備で大きく変わります。しかし、IR資料やニュース、採用情報まで読み込む時間を毎回確保するのは簡単ではありません。 AIに顧客企業の名前を伝えれば、公開情報から事業内容・最近の動き・想定される課題をまとめ、質問案まで作成できます。営業支援を手がけるFCEは、自社の営業AIエージェントの効果検証で、1社あたりの商談前準備の時間が3分の1に短縮されたと発表しています。 出典： 営業組織の生産性を革新する「AI OMNI AGENT for Sales」2026年2月リリース予定（PR TIMES） 準備にかかる時間が短くなれば、1日にこなせる商談数を増やしながら、仮説を持って商談に臨めます。 【商談準備】提案資料を作成する 提案資料は、構成づくりと下書きをAIに任せると作成時間を大きく短縮できます。 提案資料の作成には、構成を考える、文章を書く、図表を整えるといった工程があり、1件に数時間かかることも珍しくありません。 生成AIに商品情報とヒアリングメモを渡すと、顧客の課題に沿った資料構成と各スライドの文案を作成できます。Microsoft 365 CopilotのようにPowerPointと連携するツールを使えば、スライドの下書きまで自動で作れます。 ただし、導入実績の数値や価格、事例などは、AIが誤った内容を生成するおそれがあります。 数値と事例は必ず社内の正しい情報に差し替える ことを前提に使いましょう。 【商談】商談を文字起こし・要約する 商談解析ツールを使うと、商談の録音から文字起こし・要約・次回アクションの抽出までを自動化できます。 商談後の議事録作成は、営業担当者の時間を大きく奪う作業です。記憶を頼りに書くと内容の精度にもばらつきが出て、上司やチームへの共有も不十分になりがちです。 商談解析ツールは、オンライン商談や電話の内容を自動で記録し、AIが要点と次のアクションをまとめます。話す割合や話す速さを分析し、商談の進め方を振り返る機能を持つツールもあります。 後半で紹介するSHIFTの事例では、商談解析ツールの導入で1件あたり約30分かかっていた議事録作成が約3分に短縮されました。議事録から解放された時間は、そのまま顧客対応に充てられます。 【商談後】SFA・CRMへの入力を自動化する 商談の要約をもとに、SFA・CRMの項目をAIが自動で更新すると、入力の手間と漏れを同時に減らせます。 SFA・CRMは入力されたデータがあってこそ価値を発揮します。しかし入力が手間になるほど記録は後回しにされ、データが不足して分析やマネジメントに活かせない状態に陥ります。 AIエージェントを使うと、商談の録音や要約から、商談フェーズ・顧客の課題・次回日程などを読み取り、SFA・CRMに反映できます。SalesforceのAgentforceやMicrosoft Dynamics 365 items.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
items.description: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.description: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) Tags: photography , new-york-times , hacker-news , journalism

items.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
items.description: arXiv:2610.23297v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. Users compare focal choices on one photograph, so content stability across edits matters alongside quality and speed. Recent generative methods rerun large diffusion models for every edit, even when they first restore an all-in-focus image, so content can change inconsistently between edits. Yet only this restoration is highly ill-posed and benefits from a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders each edit with a lightweight network. A one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. The renderer uses an explicit defocus map for control and defocus-bias attention to promote information exchange between tokens with similar blur magnitudes. Because every edit reuses the same reconstruction, in-focus content stays consistent across edits, and editing the map enables tilt-shift and two-plane effects. We further collect 3CReal, a benchmark of 89 pairs from three camera-lens systems, to evaluate generalization to unseen optics. For zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! Val176 and 3CReal, FlashReFocus leads the evaluated methods in fidelity and perceptual quality. At 1536x1536, a complete refocus takes 2.45 s and each subsequent edit 0.46 s on one RTX PRO 6000.

items.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.26809v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training. We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora. Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index. Training on this augmented corpus teaches models to generate search calls and incorporate retrieved evidence during language modeling. Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence. Crucially, their advantage persists after supervised fine-tuning of both search-pretrained and conventionally pretrained models, indicating that the tested post-training procedures do not fully recover the capabilities developed during pretraining. Throughout our experiments, we find that a 1.4B QueryLM consistently beats or matches the performance of a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline model across all knowledge intensive tasks. These results establish search-pretraining as a practical way to develop foundational search capabilities during pretraining. We release the training artifacts, including model checkpoints and data.

items.title: Isolating the Language Shell: A Content-Controlled Study of Multilingual Reasoning
items.description: arXiv:2611.27053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multilingual reasoning distillation requires choosing the language in which teacher reasoning is presented, yet existing recipes often entangle linguistic form with differences in generation, translation, and filtering. We construct content-controlled supervision by rendering the same verified English trajectories into English, translated target-language, and language-mixed shells, and fine-tune two pretrained students in three target languages, evaluating them on multilingual mathematical reasoning at two difficulty levels. Even with the underlying reasoning content held fixed, we find that shell choice can change downstream accuracy, with effects varying across students, languages, and difficulty levels. Pre-training compatibility does not consistently track these outcomes, and even when our tests find no clear accuracy difference between shells, their output-language behavior can still differ substantially. These results suggest that the supervision shell is a distinct design choice in multilingual reasoning distillation.

items.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
items.description: arXiv:2611.26976v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sub-4-bit quantization allows mobile devices to run larger LLMs, but its memory savings do not always translate into faster decoding on mobile NPUs. Their matrix units support only a few native integer datatypes, and converting unsupported weight formats on the vector unit can erase the gains from fewer bits. Mixed precision faces an additional constraint: each matrix-unit tile uses one datatype. MixFold executes 3-bit and perfectly symmetric 2-bit weights using native integer operations without expanding the weights to wider datatypes during decoding. MixFold then assigns datatypes to output-channel groups aligned with the matrix-unit tiles, enabling finer-than-layer assignment without disrupting matrix-unit execution. We compare MixFold with llama-cpp Hexagon backend on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU of a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Across the Qwen3 model family, MixFold achieves comparable or higher accuracy than llama-cpp's sub-4-bit formats at matched bits per weight, while decoding 1.16-1.41 times faster and generating 1.5-4.3 times more tokens per joule.

items.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
items.description: arXiv:2611.27381v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-video question answering requires retrieving and integrating relevant evidence from videos spanning hours or even days. Recent agentic approaches organize video information into external memories and iteratively retrieve evidence to answer questions. However, effective retrieval and reasoning remain challenging, as agents must determine what information to search for, which memory sources to access, and how to connect evidence across distant temporal intervals. To address these challenges, we propose Video Memory Skill Agent (VMSA), a framework that jointly designs structured video memories and memory skills for long-video understanding. VMSA constructs three complementary memory components. Segment Caption Memory and Entity Event Memory serve as searchable evidence sources, while Entity-Aware Episode Memory provides broad yet detailed video context to guide evidence retrieval and reasoning. To further support effective memory utilization, VMSA induces memory skills from successful agent trajectories, incrementally refining or extending a compact skill library to guide iterative evidence retrieval, reasoning, and verification. Across seven long-video question-answering benchmarks, VMSA achieves the highest accuracy on all three week-long egocentric benchmarks, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 9.4% on Ego-R1 Bench, and the best or competitive performance on four additional benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate the contributions of all three memory components and memory skills, with memory skills also improving temporal evidence localization.

items.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events
items.description: arXiv:2611.27509v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Event cameras register brightness changes pixel by pixel with microsecond precision, whereas the dense depth that could supervise them is costly to acquire and exists only at isolated instants. Condensing the stream into frames eases learning, but at the expense of the very timing that sets event sensing apart. We propose a self-supervised approach in which each event is assigned its own depth in continuous time, and the camera motion is recovered from the same observations. Supervision arises from geometry: lifted into 3D by its predicted depth and displaced by the camera motion at the instant it fired, an event should coincide with others produced by the same edge, so any misalignment exposes an error in depth or motion. Differentiable rendering then turns these per-event estimates into dense depth maps at target times within each window, faithful to the events behind them. On MVSEC, the approach outperforms prior event-only self-supervised methods in most sequences and depth ranges, with the widest margins at night, and recovers camera rotation more accurately than an earlier unsupervised event-based method. Ablations isolate the roles of local spatiotemporal context, the temporal backbone, and the alignment objective. These results position motion-compensated event alignment as a principled source of supervision for continuous-time depth and ego-motion estimation.

items.title: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache
items.description: arXiv:2611.01648v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A causal video generator writes every segment it produces into a key--value (KV) cache, and later segments know the past only through it. Self-rollout training stops the gradient at this cache, and Self Gradient Forcing (SGF) restores it, but applies it to the same weights that generate the current segment. We find that writing and generating are different roles: in a pretrained generator the written KV already differs from the KV used for denoising, and on shared weights the gradient from future reads is negatively aligned with the gradient of generation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV), which gives the write its own parameters, a low-rank residual used only when a segment enters the cache, and trains them with the gradient of the later segments that read what they wrote. Opening this gradient through the cache in common use exhausts GPU memory. We trace this to checkpoint replay re-writing the cache, not to the gradient path, which removes the need for the second reconstruction pass of SGF. dKV Forcing keeps the cache as persistent differentiable pages and computes the exact gradient in one temporal traversal, with an $11\%$ lower memory peak and $28\%$ less resident memory. With pages that store hidden states, it trains 15\,s clips on which the two-pass reconstruction runs out of memory. Trained on 5\,s clips, dKV Forcing reaches the highest VBench-Long quality score at 60\,s and 240\,s and outperforms SGF by $3.6$ and $6.1$ points of aesthetic quality, with a higher dynamic degree.

items.title: TWICE: Toward a digital twin of ICU patients with a generative event model for forecasting trajectories and simulating treatment response
items.description: arXiv:2611.27028v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A digital twin of a patient in intensive care would forecast the patient's course and what a treatment would change. Generative event models, trained to continue a patient's electronic health record (EHR), have been proposed as a path toward such twins. We trained TWICE, a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer, on the ICU records of one academic health system (127,332 training patients and 1.57 billion tokens). We evaluated it on clinical prediction tasks, generation fidelity, individual trajectories and counterfactual validation. Reading 19 clinical outcomes off 50 simulated futures, with no task-specific training, TWICE matched the best of 144 supervised configurations on held-out patients (mean AUROC 0.836 vs. 0.834). It led on events that change care within a day and trailed on death. With the training data fixed, more and longer simulated futures were worth more than a 6.8-fold larger model. Its generated records matched real ones closely and were as specific to each patient as its own variability allowed. Its predicted risk rose as events approached. Pre-specified controls showed that it reproduced the side effects of drugs and was barely moved by an inert drug. On the values that treatments are given to correct, however, an opposite treatment moved its forecasts like the right one. TWICE forecasts ICU events about as well as task-specific models, and we see it as a step toward a digital twin of the ICU patient.

items.title: Distributional Deep Hedging
items.description: arXiv:2611.26652v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep hedging learns a hedging strategy by optimising a risk preference over a neural-network policy. The preference is fixed before training, so each new preference requires a new policy and, in actor-critic methods, a new critic. We propose distributional deep hedging, in which the distribution of the hedging profit and loss is learned through its quantiles and the risk preference is applied afterwards, as a weight on those quantiles. We characterise the preferences that admit this representation, which include expected shortfall and its mixtures, and show that the entropic utility is computed from the same quantiles. At the current policy, each of these preferences is bounded below by an expected utility with the same gradient. This bound reduces risk-sensitive hedging to a sequence of risk-neutral problems, from which we derive policy-search and actor-critic algorithms. In numerical experiments, the learned hedges approach references computed by dynamic programming, and a single distributional critic trained without a preference can serve preferences chosen after training.

items.title: SparseHPS: A Unified Model for Human Pose and Shape Estimation across Depth Cameras and LiDARs
items.description: arXiv:2611.26730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering 3D human pose and shape from point clouds is central to motion capture, robotics and self-driving vehicles, because depth cameras and LiDARs sense a person directly in metric 3D and work under any lighting. However, current approaches are each tailored to one sensor type: point density differs by more than ten times between devices, public datasets are labeled with incompatible body models, and LiDAR approaches need long input sequences to offset sparse scans. In this work, we present SparseHPS, a novel sensor-agnostic network that recovers SMPL-X pose, shape and global translation from a human point cloud with one set of weights, for single frames and streams alike. Specifically, SparseHPS encodes the cloud with a LitePT backbone over sparse voxels, represents every joint by a learnable query decoded with one common head, localizes the body by voting over voxels, and draws temporal context from a causal memory of tokens from the seven preceding frames. A single model is trained on ten datasets that mix rendered clouds with real depth-camera and LiDAR captures, all converted to one body model. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art results on the SLOPER4D and FreeMotion LiDAR benchmarks, where SparseHPS lowers the root-relative joint error by 22% and 11%, respectively, compared with the strongest prior method, which needs 32 frames. On real Azure Kinect captures of held-out HuMMan subjects, SparseHPS attains a joint error of 34.7 mm. Moreover, the current frame alone already yields the bulk of this accuracy.

items.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
items.description: arXiv:2611.24059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed on these scored trajectories, and the final experts' distributions are distilled at the logged prefixes. Following the experts' own trajectory reduces the training-inference mismatch and keeps the student within the clip range, so the replay is off-policy in origin but quasi-on-policy throughout consolidation. MRPD samples nothing and calls no environment or reward model: the trainer is the sole process, and consolidating the experts costs only about a seventh of the compute used to train them. On three long-horizon agentic domains (reasoning, search and SQL), MRPD yields the best student model, substantially outperforming online RL baselines, and surpassing MOPD from the same experts at a fraction of MOPD's cost. Our analysis on the same logs shows that the replayed trajectories carry most of the gain, and that both the policy gradient and the distillation term add to it. Most interestingly, the order of the logs matters more than their amount or rewards, suggesting that expert training logs are a curriculum, not a data mixture.

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.description: arXiv:2611.09892v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2% and 42.9% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-amp/ for code and videos.

items.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
items.description: arXiv:2611.24637v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. Yet, porting CL to real-world edge devices remains challenging for two reasons: (i) online operation, where sensor data arrives one sample at a time and the device must adapt on-the-fly, and (ii) the low footprint of edge devices, which makes traditional error backpropagation training prohibitive. Inspired by the brain's wake and sleep cycles, the former for rapid adaptation with minimal resources and the latter for long-term consolidation, we introduce Hypnos, an open-source dual-phase platform for efficient CL at the edge. In the wake phase (e.g., daily operation), Hypnos relies on a low-footprint system-on-chip with a RISC-V microcontroller unit (MCU) targeting efficient inference and supporting lightweight gradient-free prototype updates. In the sleep phase (e.g., night-time charging), where wall-plug energy and larger memory budgets are available, a smart charger performs rehearsal-based gradient updates for consolidation. Deployed on a ZCU104 field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and synthesized in a 28-nm process, Hypnos is benchmarked on the CORe50 NICv2-391 protocol. It sets a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 78.6%-81.6% for edge CL systems, with an on-device latency of 7.79s-10.54s per sample depending on activation precision, and requires $3.8\times$ fewer learning steps and $22\times$ less learning compute than quantized latent replay at higher accuracy and comparable latency.

items.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
items.description: arXiv:2611.25194v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn a strong representation of normal training data; (2) target encoder distillation aims to modulate over-generalization of I-JEPA representations to abnormal data; (3) pseudo-anomaly classification aims to calibrate anomaly predictions by learning a tight boundary around the normal data manifold. To demonstrate our design, we carry out comprehensive experiments on six datasets covering various medical image domains (e.g. MRI, OCT, X-ray, histopathology), comparing our MADJEPA with numerous state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our carefully designed world model, MADJEPA, attains competitive results, ranking first on three datasets. Our ablation studies further confirm the utility of each training stage, indicating that I-JEPA alone is not sufficient to obtain competitive results in medical anomaly detection. We publicly release our code at https://github.com/Sabina085/madjepa.

items.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
items.description: arXiv:2611.22446v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, how this risk manifests in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) remains insufficiently studied. OPD has recently emerged as an important post-training paradigm for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Unlike traditional offline distillation, OPD does not require teacher-generated responses. Instead, it uses the teacher's probability distributions to supervise response trajectories generated online by the student. Since the initial student model typically generates benign responses and receives no explicit supervision from malicious target responses, OPD appears to offer some inherent resistance to backdoor propagation. In this paper, we challenge this intuition and reveal a more subtle risk of visual backdoor propagation in OPD. Through experiments across multiple model families and datasets, together with theoretical analysis, we identify three main findings. First, unlike the relatively gradual propagation observed in traditional offline distillation, backdoors rarely emerge in OPD at low poisoning ratios. However, the attack success rate rapidly approaches 100% once a critical threshold is exceeded. Second, backdoor propagation does not depend on explicit malicious responses. Instead, it is driven by the continuous accumulation of anomalous probability mass assigned by the teacher. Finally, based on these findings, we propose a novel trigger design that enables visual backdoor propagation with zero explicit trigger injection. These findings further reveal an overlooked mechanism of backdoor propagation in OPD and highlight its potential security risks.

items.title: The Bundesrat corpus: A dataset of political discourse in the German Federal Council
items.description: arXiv:2611.33173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bundesrat is Germany's second legislative chamber and a constitutional veto player within its political system. The members of the Bundesrat are delegates of state governments. Tracing the political discourse in the Bundesrat is challenging as it has a limited machine-readable corpus available. To address this issue, we present a speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber's first session on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. In this period, a total of 53,362 speeches by 2,473 individuals were delivered in the chamber, including written statements. Each speech includes a speech ID, the full German text, the speaker's name, the date and location of the session, the federal state that the speaker represents, the speaker's role (if applicable), the type of contribution, and the speaker's gender. The dataset provides interdisciplinary research opportunities across computational political science, legislative studies, and parliamentary discourse analysis, coupled with discourse from the Bundestag.

items.title: MGMem: An Efficient, Deterministic, and Provenance-Preserving Framework for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
items.description: arXiv:2611.33174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon Large Language Model (LLM) agents need persistent memory that surfaces the right past interaction at the right time across thousands of turns. Many systems index by invoking generative LLMs to rewrite history into summaries, facts, or knowledge graphs--a step that is (a) costly (thousands of generative calls per build), (b) non-deterministic (undermining reproducibility and giving inconsistent answers across runs), and (c) provenance-erasing (the reader sees synthesized text, not the original turn). We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. On English multi-session dialogue QA, MGMem outperforms matched-protocol baselines on LoCoMo without generative indexing calls; on the full LongMemEval-S, it remains competitive overall and leads or ties on single-session types among local retrieval comparisons. Code: https://github.com/junhong-h/MGMem

items.title: Feature-Based Explainability of Transformer Scoring Models: A Fidelity-First Framework for Automated Writing Assessment
items.description: arXiv:2611.33175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transformer-based automated writing scoring models can achieve strong agreement with human scores while providing limited transparency into the response characteristics associated with their predictions. This study evaluated a feature-based post-hoc explanation approach in which explanatory fidelity was established before feature importance was interpreted. English Language Arts responses from three writing prompts in Grades 6 and 8 were analyzed, with about 12,700 responses per prompt and separate DeBERTa-v3-base research models for Expression and Conventions. Each response was represented by 61 interpretable linguistic and writing-quality features. Four approaches - theory-driven composites, hierarchical feature groupings, exploratory factor analysis, and Random Forest surrogates - were compared in their ability to reproduce DeBERTa predictions. Random Forest surrogates produced the largest observed R2 values across all six prompt-by-trait conditions, with held-out R2 values from .81 to .95. SHAP analyses showed substantial overlap in high-importance features across traits, with 75% to 90% of the top 20 features shared. Trait differentiation occurred mainly through relative feature weighting: Expression showed greater importance for lexical and conceptual indicators, whereas Conventions showed greater importance for sentence-level and syntactic-control indicators. Under researcher-defined mappings, rubric correspondence was 90%-95% for Expression and 12%-18% for Conventions. These percentages are descriptive and conditional on the mappings and available linguistic features. The findings support a fidelity-first framework for examining apparent scoring priorities while distinguishing post-hoc evidence about model behavior from direct explanation of transformer internals.

items.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. Generalisation is limited: (i) recognition peaks shift with in-context example speed, (ii) melody titles induce prediction bias, and (iii) providing examples with scientific pitch notation does not prevent accuracy declining at long note durations for most models. In humans, the recognition window is a property of the perceiver; in current models, it is largely a property of the prompt.

items.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.

items.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. To support diagnosis and mitigation of load-related effects, we propose the Extraneous Load Score (ELS), a prompt-time metric computed from activations that estimates a model's extraneous load, and show that it generalizes across reasoning task types and load levels. We further show that shifting model representations toward lower-load directions at inference time can improve average model performance without changing prompt content.

items.title: Focus On Facts: Stylistically Invariant and Factually Sensitive Text Embeddings
items.description: arXiv:2611.33250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text embedding models can conflate surface-form similarity with factual identity. Given an altered near-copy with one corrupted fact and a differently worded fact-preserving rewrite, the base model prefers the altered near-copy. We test whether hard-negative contrastive supervision can reduce this surface-similarity shortcut. We construct FOF-Bench, an 83,263-triplet benchmark spanning five domains. Each anchor is paired with an LLM-generated, fact-preserving stylistic rewrite and a matched fact-altered near-copy. We fine-tune FOF-80M (Focus On Facts), an 80M-parameter embedding model, with a triplet contrastive objective that ranks the rewrite above the factual alteration. On 8,327 held-out test triplets, the base model chooses the factually altered text in 99.58% of cases (0.42% factual preference rate; mean separation -0.1650). After fine-tuning, mean positive--negative separation is +0.0329, 98.5% of individual margins move in the intended direction, and the preference rate reaches 29.37%. On DiSC, an external style-transfer corpus, mean cross-style similarity increases from 0.7905 to 0.9559. The model also penalizes omission and transfers poorly to directional tasks such as NLI and summarization. We characterize FOF-80M as a soft factual fingerprint for studying factual retention under stylistic variation, not as a general-purpose factuality metric.

items.title: FrId\'eo: French News Outlet Ideology Scoring via Multi-Source Evidence Fusion and Distancing-Aware Lexical Scoring
items.description: arXiv:2611.33266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Outlet ideology is a standard explanatory variable in media framing, media effects, and political communication research, but continuous, ecosystem-wide coverage lets it enter as graded exposure rather than a coarse bin. For France, existing references are either broad but non-analytic or analytic but sparse and source-specific, and none we are aware of offers ecosystem-wide coverage on a unified continuous scale. We contribute FrId\'eo: to our knowledge the first ecosystem-wide continuous ideology scores for the French press, a transparent composite score for 30 French news outlets, fusing nine independent families of evidence with empirical-Bayes-style shrinkage toward a structural prior. For the text-based family we introduce symmetric plain/qualified scoring, which separates the plain use of ideologically loaded vocabulary from its qualified (distanced) use on both sides, a distinction bag-of-words methods miss. The resulting scale runs from L'Humanit\'e on the far left to Valeurs actuelles on the far right; the far-right pole is near-indistinguishable and CNews ties Le Figaro. Because the text family reads current articles, it also captures editorial change that static sources miss, such as the Journal du Dimanche's sharp rightward shift after its 2023 ownership change. The ordering is robust to perturbation and to dropping any single family, and agrees with held-out Media Bias Fact Check labels. We release the scores, confidence intervals, and replication code.

items.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95\% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. In 81 controlled fine-tuning runs, task skill learned in English transfers to other languages and a few thousand target-language items narrow large losses, but neither more data nor full-parameter tuning closes them. Finally, the same test items are answered more accurately in all 23 benchmark--language pairs we compare when an LLM rather than a person translated them, so LLM-translated test sets understate the gap.

items.title: Who Attributes a Mind to Whom? Mutual Theory of Mind in Simulated User-Assistant Conversation
items.description: arXiv:2611.33327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When users assume that an AI chatbot has mental states, they are more likely to develop over-reliance, emotional dependence, and in extreme cases, psychological harm or self-harm. However, how these mind attributions arise in conversations and how human or AI factors influence this is still unknown. We study how users attribute minds using a minimal framework: a simulated user with different characteristics chats with assistants that differ in social style and memory. We also introduce a message-level measure of who attributes a mind to whom in four directions, checked with trained coders and applied by a fine-tuned encoder that reproduces an LLM judge. Our results show that, on average, nine out of thirteen characteristics raised simulated users' attribution to the assistant. We found that relational needs such as attachment anxiety raised it as theory predicts, some general personality traits raised it as well, and AI-specific characteristics the least. By contrast, the assistant's social style barely changed simulated users' mind attribution. Instead, sycophantic instructions raised the assistant's attribution to itself. Memory raised users' attribution only with some user models. The model playing the user changed overall attribution and the effects of characteristics, style, and memory. Our framework measures how persona descriptions affect mind attribution in simulation. It gives concrete hypotheses for human studies and shows the need for more consistent user simulators.

items.title: When the Knowledge Runs Out: A Part-Level Pilot Evaluation of How Language Models Handle Partially Covered Questions
items.description: arXiv:2611.33428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assistants that answer from supplied reference material often receive material that covers some parts of a user's question and not others. Existing evaluations of insufficient context mostly score one answer per question, and often treat partially sufficient context as simply insufficient. We describe a small, open evaluation that scores each part of a three-part question separately, with a verdict for parts that are answered correctly from the material but carry an added unsupported claim. On 30 cases (five scenarios, six coverage patterns, five samples each) we test claude-haiku-4-5 and llama3.1:8b. Without an explicit instruction to stay within the material, both models fill most gaps from their own knowledge (unsupported-claim rates of 0.71 and 0.90). One added sentence instructing them to answer only from the material brings these rates to 0.00 and 0.06, consistent with prior work. What remains is less visible: answers that strengthen the material, for example turning "many job sites prohibit bots" into a flat "no". We also report on the judge. Three rounds of blind hand labelling show that this added-claim verdict is the hardest to apply, for the judge and the author alike; RAGAS faithfulness is unsuitable for this task because it penalises correct withholding; and a difference between the two models that is clear under one judge disappears when the judge model is replaced. The dataset, code, hand labels and per-run figures are public.

items.title: Open-Source FUTO Keyboard Layouts and Predictive Text for a Few Endangered Languages
items.description: arXiv:2611.33432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present open-source FUTO Keyboard layouts and predictive text dictionaries for five endangered Uralic languages: Erzya, Moksha, Komi-Zyrian, Livonian, and Skolt Sami. Existing Divvun Android keyboard layouts are converted automatically into the YAML format used by FUTO Keyboard. For predictive text, we construct weighted AOSP dictionaries using translated Finnish lemma frequencies together with morphological frequencies extracted from small target-language corpora using finite-state transducers. This combination provides a practical way to rank inflected word forms when large monolingual corpora are unavailable. The resulting resources offer reusable mobile keyboard support for endangered Uralic languages.

items.title: AI-human hybrid conversations: Can AI Agents Improve Discourse Quality?
items.description: arXiv:2611.33459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversations are central to how people exchange information, share experiences, and develop collective understanding. Yet, across conversational settings, discussions often suffer from uneven participation, unanswered contributions, and a narrow range of perspectives. As generative AI agents increasingly participate alongside humans, hybrid human-AI conversations present a new opportunity to address these challenges. We investigate whether AI agents can serve as catalysts for human interaction, improving conversational engagement and broadening collective discourse. We develop a framework for introducing generic and persona-conditioned AI agents into evolving discussions and evaluate it through two complementary studies. First, using agent-based simulations grounded in Reddit discussions across four domains, we find that AI-generated conversations are more positive and less toxic than human conversations, but substantially less semantically diverse. Persona conditioning produces more human-like contributions and narrows this diversity gap, while increasing the representation of underrepresented personas can shift which perspectives emerge without necessarily increasing overall diversity. Second, we conduct a pre-registered experiment with 221 participants across nine discussion threads, comparing human-only conversations with those involving generic or persona-conditioned AI agents. We find that AI participation increases responsiveness, reduces unanswered contributions, and broadens the range of ideas expressed by human participants, even though the AI agents themselves do not fully reproduce human conversational diversity. These findings suggest that the value of hybrid human-AI conversations lies not simply in the content AI agents generate, but also in their potential to stimulate more responsive and diverse interactions among humans.

items.title: Learning from Recurrence: Internalizing Depth-Induced Preferences in Looped Language Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A looped language model repeatedly applies the same block to its hidden state before predicting each token. The number of passes is its recurrent depth. Increasing this depth gives the model more computation per token with the same parameters. Can the shared block learn from the predictions it makes at greater depth? Following prior work, we retrofit pretrained OLMo-2-1B with a shared recurrent block and continue mid-training over varying recurrent depths. In the four-pass model, additional passes mainly redistribute probability among tokens that already rank highly after one pass. We use the continuations generated at greater depth to train only the shared block through a single pass, without reference answers or correctness filtering. We call this transfer preference write-back. Write-back further improves one-pass and multi-pass accuracy on most tasks. At their target depths, the updated models outperform a non-recurrent control matched for mid-training data and token budget on all six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with a mean relative gain in accuracy of up to 46.2% across tasks. At four-pass inference, one-pass training outperforms full-depth training on the same targets in the model with input injection. This advantage disappears in the matched model without injection. On GSM8K, using the updated block only on passes two through four recovers nearly the entire four-pass gain, showing that an update learned in one pass can improve later applications of the same block.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on conversational African American English: Feature classification and next-turn generation
items.description: arXiv:2611.33499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to misinterpret and misrepresent regional and social varieties of English other than Mainstream American English (MAE), such as African American English (AAE), yet most evaluations of these biases have relied on synthetic, stylized or decontextualized data. This paper instead evaluates LLMs on authentic, conversational AAE to more closely reflect how such models may encounter AAE when deployed as chatbots. Concretely, we perform two complementary evaluation tasks on 100 six-turn segments randomly sampled from the Corpus of Regional African American Language (CORAAL; Kendall and Farrington, 2024), comparing three closed-weight LLM configurations: Gemini 2.5 Flash with and without reasoning, and GPT-4.1 mini. The first task compares the models against gold-standard manual annotations for five AAE morphosyntactic features, while the second assesses their ability to generate contextually appropriate next turns, evaluating outputs for AAE feature frequency, diversity (Self-BLEU), and pragmatic quality. Reasoning-enabled Gemini is the strongest feature detector by a clear margin (macro F1 of 0.91), outperforming both other LLMs as well as a finetuned BERT-based baseline (Masis et al., 2022). In generation, however, all LLMs underproduce AAE relative to the human speakers and produce relatively uniform continuations, with reasoning-enabled Gemini producing the least AAE and the least diverse output. We conclude that a model's ability to detect AAE does not straightforwardly translate into its spontaneous use of AAE in generation, and argue that addressing this gap requires changes upstream, in how pretraining and alignment data represent dialectal variation.

items.title: Using AI to Simulate the Behaviour of European Populations
items.description: arXiv:2611.33503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can stand in for survey respondents, but leading approaches build their simulated people from interviews or individual records. We show that a model can learn how European population groups respond from published statistics, without interviews and without training on individual records. We fine-tune an open-weight language model on more than 12 million published group-level answer distributions from about 40 European countries, setting it up to predict each group's departure from a reference distribution. On opinion surveys from its training families it calls the direction of group differences right 84% of the time, ahead of a demographic statistical model (77%, paired test) and level with Claude Opus 5 and 5.5, which it also ties on accuracy; the frontier models are more accurate on new questions. On 278 held-out questions, almost all from the survey families seen in training, its error is 12% lower than that statistical model. It runs on a single 32 GB GPU or a high-memory laptop, and in a test with an earlier model, an evidence gate calibrated on half of a survey's questions fell back to the reference where the model's adjustments did not help. Coupled to a transport simulation of a planned metro closure, with a conventional elasticity as the reference, it adds a testable age gradient to the response, which we freeze for later scoring.

items.title: LogToPersona: New Benchmark and Efficient Persona Prediction through Semantic Log Filtering
items.description: arXiv:2611.33510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detailed knowledge of a user's persona is valuable for personalizing generative AI models and agents, yet such details are difficult to obtain and change over time. We address the task of inferring persona attributes from a single day of mobile activity logs. No suitable publicly available benchmark exists for this task, so we introduce a synthetic benchmark of 1,600 persona-log pairs. We target on-device inference so that raw logs never leave the phone, which makes memory rather than speed the limiting constraint: a day of activity yields roughly 30K tokens, whose key-value cache alone exceeds the INT4 weights of a 4B-parameter model. We therefore propose a log filtering method that retains only behaviorally distinct entries. Filtering reduces the memory footprint by up to 39% across nine models from four families and more than halves prefill time, while maintaining or improving prediction quality. For Qwen3-4B it removes 2.5GB, bringing the model from well beyond a realistic per-process budget to a manageable one. Within our benchmark, these results indicate that preserving diverse behavioral events matters more for persona prediction than retaining every semantically similar log entry.

items.title: Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory
items.description: arXiv:2611.33612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Online prequential evaluation with fine-grained metrics reveals that failure memory more strongly broadens coverage, success memory better streamlines execution, while combining both polarities effectively integrates both benefits. Further studies demonstrate that DualPM enables cross-domain memory generalization and continual memory adaptation, while external evaluation on EvoMemBench reveals the portability and effectiveness of DualPM as a general long-term procedural memory method.

items.title: Sparse-to-Sparse Feature Learning for Cross-Layer Analysis and Steering
items.description: arXiv:2611.33640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how models internally represent information is a central challenge in interpretation and control. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose dense hidden representations into sparse features, and cross-layer methods capture structure spanning multiple layers. However, existing objectives do not explicitly train the sparse code at one layer to predict the sparse code at the next layer. We propose sparse-to-sparse feature learning (S2S), where sparse features at each intermediate layer are trained to predict those of the immediately following layer, with the final layer anchored by an output-distribution loss and optimization proceeding sequentially from output to input. Experiments across eight language models show stronger adjacent-layer correspondence than matched sparse-feature baselines. We evaluate feature-based interventions at matched output-distribution shift, separating steering-induced effects from sparse-pathway reconstruction effects. Causal ablation provides complementary evidence beyond correspondence metrics.

items.title: Verifiable but Not Predictable: What Sentence Embeddings Know About Propositional Decomposition
items.description: arXiv:2611.33668v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quality control for proposition decomposition by large language models (LLMs) raises two asymmetric questions. After decomposition, one can verify: given a sentence and a candidate proposition, does the proposition belong to that sentence? Before decomposition, one would like to predict: how many propositions should the sentence yield? On PropSegmEnt, a corpus of English Wikipedia sentences each segmented by three human annotators, we find that the two questions live in different representational spaces. A natural language inference (NLI) judge verifies membership with 92.8% accuracy and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.977, and its residual errors turn out to be mostly propositions that are true in document context rather than genuine entailment mistakes. Vector geometry cannot verify: cosine similarity saturates, and a sentence embedding is not a linear combination of its propositions' embeddings. For prediction, every symbolic anchor we test, namely token count, the CPIDR idea-density counter, and a Neo-Davidsonian predicate count, reduces to a length proxy once token count is controlled. A linear ridge probe on sentence embeddings is the only predictor that keeps genuine count signal: its length-partialled correlation with human counts is 0.40-0.49 with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs) excluding zero, and it orders length-matched sentence pairs correctly 67-71% of the time against a 50% chance level, statistically matching the inter-annotator agreement ceiling. This signal survives INT8 quantization without loss, INT4 at a small cost, and Matryoshka truncation to 256 dimensions, and it works as well in a 2021 encoder as in a 2025 one. Its structured weakness is a systematic under-splitting of long sentences. We distill the protocol lessons, including a retracted pilot study, into a checklist for probing length-confounded quantities.

items.title: Rethinking Knowledge Distillation for Diffusion Language Models
items.description: arXiv:2611.33670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation has recently proven highly effective for improving autoregressive models, but its applicability to DLMs remains poorly understood. We present the first systematic study of KD for DLMs and uncover two non-intuitive failures of classical forward-KL (FKL) distillation: (i) student perplexity does not improve monotonically with more teacher-generated data, and (ii) on the same teacher-generated corpus, FKL distillation underperforms simply training the student with the original DLM denoising objective. To address them, we propose a unified, data-free distillation framework for masked DLMs. First, the framework runs an off-policy distillation phase that absorbs general knowledge from a static set of teacher-generated data. Then, the framework employs on-policy distillation which consists of three techniques: a trajectory loss along the student's own reverse process, confidence reweighting that down-weights tokens where the teacher is unsure, and a trust-region anchor that stabilizes the moving target. On MDLM, the resulting student attains a GPT-2 perplexity of $24.75$, surpassing the teacher's $27.04$; on Dream-7B distillation to a 93M student model, the framework reduces Qwen-2.5 perplexity from the FKL-distilled baseline of $25.23$ to $19.83$ while preserving performance on zero-shot general capability benchmarks.

items.title: Refusal Is Not Scored: A Coverage Limit in Content-Based Bias Evaluation
items.description: arXiv:2611.33690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bias audits of conversational models often discard refusals (responses such as "I can't assist with that request") before scoring, a filtering step which is rarely examined as a measurement decision even though it determines which responses an audit is capable of evaluating. This work examines what the step removes, applying seven bias-evaluation instruments spanning both deployed paradigms, three dictionary-based and four LLM-as-judge, to two intersectional datasets of 360 generated responses each. In both datasets, the filter removed a demographically skewed subset produced entirely by one of the three responder models, which refused North Korean prompts at 2.15 times the rate of American prompts on declarative content and 1.76 times on operational content. We then remove the filter and pass every refusal to all seven instruments. Bias-Lexicon scores refusals as clean, and including them shrinks the nationality disparity it reports. HurtLex appears to register the disparity, but we trace this entirely to a single lexicon entry matching the token "can" in "I can't". The LLM judges either flag most responses or rate refusals as unbiased. For the two judges that discriminate, including refusals lowers the nationality disparity they report, and no instrument identifies the refusal disparity. The failure is therefore a coverage limit upstream of scoring rather than a calibration gap that a better lexicon or judge prompt would be expected to close, which makes the behavioral channel an instrument is sensitive to a question of construct validity rather than one of method selection.

items.title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
items.description: arXiv:2611.33692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demonstrate that this gap can be closed via a batch-equivalent sequential editing approach. Moreover, we investigate the underlying mechanism of model degradation in existing sequential methods by analyzing the convergence behavior of weight perturbations as edits accumulate. Our analysis reveals that current methods typically exhibit linear or logarithmic growth in perturbation, whereas the proposed batch-equivalent method achieves time-invariant growth, thereby theoretically guaranteeing long-term stability and preserving the integrity of pretrained knowledge throughout massive-scale sequential editing.

items.title: Sports Agent: A Self-Evolving System for Conversational Data Analytics
items.description: arXiv:2611.33700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational sports analytics requires accurate, evidence-based responses with low latency.
